 Game Notes: Canucks at Sharks
 By 
 Canucks Communications 
 Vancouver Canucks 
 October 29, 2026 
 Link copied 
 CANUCKS AT SHARKS 
 TV: Sportsnet, NBC Sports California
 Radio: KiSS West Coast
 MATCH-UP INFO 
 Tonight marks the first of four meetings between the Canucks and Sharks this season: Oct. 29 (road), Dec. 14 (road), Dec. 19 (home), and Apr. 3 (home).  
 Vancouver is 73-59-9-7 all-time against San Jose, including a 39-31-5-2 record on the road.
 The Canucks are 6-4-0 in their last 10 games against the Sharks (2-3-0 in their last five).
 Elias Pettersson leads active Canucks skaters in scoring against San Jose with 23 points (8-18-26) in 26 career games.  
 In 30 career games against the Sharks, Brock Boeser has 23 points (13-10-23).
 Jake DeBrusk has 15 points (8-7-15) in 17 career games against San Jose.
 In 19 career games against the Sharks, Filip Hronek has 15 points (4-11-15).
 Kevin Lankinen is 4-2-0 with a 3.42 goals-against average and an .880 save percentage in six career games against San Jose.
 Leevi Meriläinen has yet to face the Sharks in his career.  
 QUICK NUMBERS 
 Elias Pettersson ranks tied for fifth in the NHL in power play goals (4).
 In his last four games against San Jose, Filip Hronek has five points (1-4-5).
 D Elias Pettersson ranks fifth amongst all defencemen in hits (35).
 LAST MEETING – APR. 11/26: VAN 4 at SJS 3 (SO) 
 Igor Chernyshov opened the scoring with 3:41 left in the first…Marco Rossi tied the game 5:56 into the second…Victor Mancini had the lone assist…Tyler Toffoli gave the Sharks the lead 3:06 later…Jake DeBrusk tied the game with 2:23 left in the middle frame…Filip Hronek and Elias Pettersson had the helpers…Chernyshov gave San Jose the lead 12:44 into the third…Teddy Blueger evened the game with 3:00 remaining in the third…Linus Karlsson had the only assist…Karlsson scored the shootout winner in the sixth round…DeBrusk had eight shots…Nils Höglander had three hits…Marcus Pettersson, Liam Öhgren, and Rossi each blocked two shots…Kevin Lankinen made 28 saves through 65 minutes and five in the shootout.

 LAST GAME PLAYED – OCT. 27/26: VAN 6 at ANA 5 (OT) 
 A.J. Greer opened the scoring for Anaheim with 4:08 remaining in the first…Liam Öhgren tied the game 6:36 into the second…Linus Karlsson and Zeev Buium had the assists…Jeff Malott re-took the lead for the Ducks 30 seconds later…Beckett Sennecke doubled the lead with a power play goal at 15:44…Leo Carlsson added another with 1:36 left in the middle frame…Brock Boeser got Vancouver within two with an unassisted goal at 11:40 of the third…Greer got one back for the Ducks 43 seconds later…Jamie Oleksiak responded for Vancouver 31 seconds later…Boeser and Elias Pettersson were awarded the assists…Jonathan Lekkerimäki got the Canucks within one at 17:14 of the third…Lekkerimäki tied the game with 1:57 left in regulation…Pettersson and Filip Hronek had the helpers…Hronek scored the game-winner on the power play with 11 seconds remaining in overtime…Boeser and Lekkerimäki recorded the assists…Boeser and Karlsson each had six shots…D Elais Pettersson had six hits…Filip Chytil blocked two shots...Leevi Meriläinen made 18 saves.

 ON THIS DATE 
 The Canucks have played 14 times on October 29 in the franchise’s history, going 6-3-3-2.
 This includes a 2-1-1-2 record on the road.
 The Canucks have yet to face San Jose on October 29 in the franchise’s history.   
 LEKKER-MÄGIC 
 Scoring two goals in 49 seconds to tie the game on Oct. 27/26 at ANA, Jonathan Lekkerimäki scored the fastest two goals by a single Canucks player since Pius Suter (23 seconds) on Apr. 8/25 at DAL.
 This was Lekkerimäki’s first career multi-goal game, and first career three-point game (2-1-3).
 MULTI-POINT PETEY 
 Recording two assists in the third period on Oct. 27/26 at ANA, Elias Pettersson recorded his 21st career multi-assist period, tying Brendan Morrison for the 10th most in franchise history.
 With two assists on Oct. 27/26 at ANA, Elias Pettersson passed Trevor Linden and Andre Boudrias for the seventh-most multi-assist games in franchise history (69).
 NEVER SAY NEVER 
 Despite trailing by three goals in the third period on Oct. 27/26 at ANA, the Canucks mounted a third period comeback and won the game in overtime, becoming the first team this season to record a three goal, third period comeback.
 This was the sixth three goal, third period comeback in franchise history, and first since Apr. 8/25 at DAL (6-5 OTW).
 BROCKSTAR 
 Registering a goal and two assists on Oct. 27/26 at ANA, Brock Boeser passed Don Lever for the 13th most games recording at least one goal and one assist in franchise history (57).
 This was also Boeser’s 31st career three-point game, passing Patrik Sundstrom for the 13th most three-point games in franchise history.
 Bringing Vancouver within two on Oct. 25/26 vs MIN, Brock Boeser tied Tony Tanti (147) for the eighth-most even-strength goals in franchise history.
 Passed on Oct. 27/26 at ANA.
 With an assist on Elias Pettersson’s power play goal on Oct. 17/26 at TBL, Brock Boeser tied Brendan Morrison for 15th on the Canucks all-time power play assist list (90). 
 Passed on Oct. 20/26 vs CAR.
 Recording an assist on Oct. 17/26 at TBL, Brock Boeser tied Todd Bertuzzi for 13th on the Canucks all-time assist list (261).
 Passed on Oct. 20/26 vs CAR.
 MOVIN’ ON UP 
 Recording the primary assist on Max Sasson’s third period goal on Oct. 25/26, Filip Hronek passed Tyler Myers for 17th on the Canucks all-time points list by a defenceman (139).
 Assisting on Elias Pettersson’s first period goal on Oct. 22/26 vs DET, Filip Hronek passed Dan Hamhuis for sole possession of 14th on the Canucks all-time assists list by a defenceman (120).
 With an assist on Oct. 3/26 vs CGY, Elias Pettersson passed Alex Edler for eighth on the franchise’s all-time assist list (311).
 POWER PETEY 
 Doubling the Canucks lead on Oct. 17/26 at TBL via a power play goal, Elias Pettersson tied Greg Adams for 10th on the Canucks all-time power play goals list (65).
 Pettersson passed Greg Adams on Oct. 22/26 vs DET.
 Via his power play goal on Oct. 1726 at TBL, Elias Pettersson tied Alex Edler for the eighth-most power play points in franchise history (177).
 Pettersson passed Alex Edler on Oct. 22/26 vs DET.
 G-PETEY 
 Doubled Vancouver’s lead on Oct. 15/26 at FLA, D Elias Pettersson tied his career-high in goals (3), set in 2025.26.
 Tying the game on Oct. 11/26 at NYR, D Elias Pettersson notched his first career shorthanded goal, becoming the fourth Canucks defenceman in the last decade to record a shorthanded goal.
 Scoring his first goal of the season on Oct. 3/26 vs CGY, D Elias Pettersson recorded his first career game-winning goal.
 READY TO BROCK & ROLL 
 Entering 2026.27, Brock Boeser is close to moving up the franchise list in a number of different categories:
 Tied with Todd Bertuzzi for fifth on the Canucks all-time power play goals list (79).
 Passed on Oct. 13/26 at NYI
 Tied with J.T. Miller for 10th on the Canucks all-time power play points list (165).
 Passed on Sept. 29/26 at EDM
 One assist behind Brendan Morrison for 14th on the Canucks all-time assists list (257).
 Tied on Sept. 29/26 at EDM
 Passed on Oct. 1/26 vs EDM
 Two goals behind Tony Tanti for eighth on the Canucks all-time even-strength goals list (147). 
 SWEDE START TO THE SEASON 
 Recording an assist on Oct. 20/26 vs CAR, Elias Pettersson extended his season-opening home assist streak to four games, tied for the fourth-longest streak to begin a season in franchise history (H. Sedin: 5 games in 2010.11, Hronek: 6 games in 2023.24, Gradin 8 games in 1983.84).
 With two points (0-2-2) on Oct. 8/26 at CAR, Elias Pettersson extended his season-opening point streak to five games (2-6-8), tied for the longest of his career and tied for the eighth-longest season-opening point streak in franchise history.
 CZECH OUT FIL 
 Assisting on Paul Cotter’s goal on Oct. 4/26 vs VGK, Filip Hronek tied Doug Halward (118) for 15th on the Canucks all-time assist list by a defenceman.
 With his first of two assists on Oct. 1/26 vs EDM, Filip Hronek passed Michal Rozsival for the eighth-most assists by a Czech-born defenceman in NHL history (240).
 Recording two points (0-2-2) on Oct. 1/26 vs EDM, Filip Hronek tied Jaroslav Spacek (58) for the fifth-most multipoint games by a Czech defenceman in NHL history.
 Notching two assists on Oct. 1/26 vs EDM, Filip Hronek tied Marek Zidlicky for the fourth-most multi-assist games by a Czech defenceman in NHL history (45).
 BETTER CALL PAUL 
 Opening the scoring on Oct. 4/26 vs VGK, Paul Cotter notched his fourth goal in his fourth game as a Canuck, matching Curt Fraser (1978), Elias Pettersson (2018) and Tyler Toffoli (2020) for the second-most goals scored by a player in their first four games as a Canuck.
 Making his first appearance in a Canucks uniform on Sept. 29/26 at EDM, Paul Cotter achieved a number of franchise marks, including:
 First player to score a shorthanded goal in his Canucks debut.
 First player to score the overtime winner in his Canucks debut.
 Scoring two goals in his Canucks debut, Paul Cotter became the sixth player in franchise history to score multiple goals in his team debut, joining Claire Alexander, Thomas Gradin, Greg Adams, Esa Tikkanen, and Elias Lindholm.
 With both a shorthanded goal and overtime winner on Sept. 29.26 at EDM, Paul Cotter became the second player in NHL history to record both such goals in a season opener.
 MAMMA MIA! PETEY’S PLAYING THE HITS ALL NIGHT LONG 
 With eight hits on Oct. 3/26 vs CGY, Elias Pettersson has 16 hits over a two-game span (Oct. 1-3/26), the most hits he has registered in a two-game span in his career.
 THREE-POINT PETEY 
 Registering three points (1-2-3) on Oct. 1/26 vs EDM, Elias Pettersson passed Thomas Gradin for sole possession of the seventh-most three-point games in franchise history (39).
 DOWN BUT NOT OUT 
 Scoring shorthanded to open the scoring during their season opener courtesy of Paul Cotter, the 2026.27 Canucks became the second team in franchise history to score their first goal of the season shorthanded, joining the 2000.01 Canucks (Matt Cooke).
 NEW MAN(NY) IN TOWN 
 Hired as the 23rd Head Coach in franchise history on June 1, 2026, Manny Malhotra became the eighth coach in the last 30 years to win the Calder Cup with an organization’s AHL affiliate (as the Head Coach) before being promoted to the NHL club as Head Coach.
 First since Sheldon Keefe (Toronto Marlies and Maple Leafs).
